agenda: The situation in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to secure Security Council backing for new, credible presidential elections, validate the constitutional authority of the democratically elected National Assembly, and mandate unhindered access for international humanitarian aid. We anticipate strong resistance and potential vetoes from the Russian Federation and China, who view any criticism of the May 2018 elections or recognition of the National Assembly's primacy as infringement upon Venezuelan sovereignty and foreign intervention. Securing the necessary nine affirmative votes will also require carefully reassuring non-aligned Council members on respect for territorial integrity and adherence to international humanitarian principles.

messages.Belgium: Belgium fully supports the draft resolution, which reflects our deep concern for the suffering of the Venezuelan people and the urgent need for a peaceful, democratic solution through free, fair, and credible presidential elections. We welcome the focus on unhindered humanitarian access and emphasize that all humanitarian aid must strictly adhere to the core principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence. Belgium stands ready to vote in favor of this text.
messages.China: China strictly adheres to the principle of non-interference in internal affairs and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. The current draft text blatantly interferes in Venezuela's domestic affairs by delegitimizing its government, attempting to impose external regime change, and politicizing humanitarian issues. Unless the text is thoroughly overhauled to respect Venezuela's sovereignty and uphold the constitutional authority of the legitimate government, China will have no choice but to vote against it.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the core objectives of the draft resolution, notably the urgent need to address the humanitarian crisis and restore democratic constitutional order through free and fair elections. Having experienced the vital role of the international community during our own post-electoral crisis, we believe that an inclusive political dialogue is essential to achieving a peaceful, lasting solution. We also underscore that humanitarian assistance must remain strictly depoliticized and guided by core humanitarian principles.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United States. As a nation in the region deeply affected by the Venezuelan crisis, we emphasize the urgent necessity of restoring constitutional democracy through free, fair, and credible presidential elections, as well as guaranteeing immediate and unhindered access for humanitarian assistance to alleviate the suffering of the Venezuelan people.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea emphasizes that the Security Council must strictly respect the Charter principles of national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and non-interference in the internal affairs of Member States. The political and constitutional future of Venezuela belongs solely to the Venezuelan people through inclusive, peaceful dialogue without external imposition or regime change rhetoric. We cannot support provisions that delegitimize national authorities, single out specific institutions, or politicize humanitarian assistance.
messages.France: France fully supports this draft resolution, which responds to the urgent humanitarian and political crisis in Venezuela by calling for free, fair, and credible presidential elections and the protection of the National Assembly. We appreciate the penholder's focus on unhindered humanitarian access and would welcome explicit reference to the fundamental humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence to ensure aid is delivered strictly on the basis of needs. We stand ready to vote in favor of this text.
messages.Germany: Germany fully supports this draft resolution, which addresses the grave humanitarian crisis and the urgent need to restore constitutional and democratic order in Venezuela. We stand firmly behind the democratically elected National Assembly and call for free, fair, and credible presidential elections. We appreciate the draft's clear emphasis on humanitarian principles and the delivery of unhindered humanitarian aid to the suffering Venezuelan people.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia is deeply concerned by the worsening humanitarian and socioeconomic situation facing the Venezuelan people. However, Council action must strictly adhere to the UN Charter principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and non-interference in internal affairs, while ensuring humanitarian aid is not politicized and complies with General Assembly resolution 46/182. A durable solution can only be achieved through an inclusive, peaceful, Venezuelan-led and Venezuelan-owned political dialogue without external imposition.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait remains deeply alarmed by the severe humanitarian and economic conditions affecting the Venezuelan people, and we support efforts to facilitate humanitarian access and advance a peaceful, democratic political resolution. We place particular importance on ensuring that all humanitarian operations strictly adhere to international humanitarian principles and General Assembly resolution 46/182, avoiding politicization. We encourage the penholder to emphasize peaceful dialogue and the Secretary-General's good offices in line with the UN Charter.
messages.Peru: Peru fully supports this draft resolution, which reflects the urgent need to address the deep humanitarian, political, and institutional crisis in Venezuela. As a country bearing the direct impact of the mass exodus of Venezuelan citizens and as an active member of the Lima Group, we believe the Security Council must act decisively to uphold the constitutional authority of the National Assembly and ensure the unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian aid. We commend the penholder for aligning the text with regional efforts to facilitate a peaceful, Venezuelan-led return to constitutional democracy through free and fair presidential elections.
messages.Poland: Poland fully supports the draft resolution presented by the United States. The text accurately reflects the critical humanitarian and political crisis in Venezuela and upholds the legitimacy of the democratically elected National Assembly. We stand firmly with our European partners and allies in calling for unhindered humanitarian access and a peaceful path toward free and fair presidential elections.
messages.Russian Federation: This draft resolution is an unacceptable attempt to weaponize the Security Council for regime change and external meddling in the domestic affairs of a sovereign Member State. Artificially manufactured pretexts regarding humanitarian assistance cannot be used to justify political subversion or the threat of military intervention against the legitimate government of President Nicolás Maduro. Unless the text is thoroughly overhauled to respect Venezuela's sovereignty, constitutional order, and the UN Charter, the Russian Federation cannot allow it to pass.
messages.South Africa: South Africa is deeply committed to upholding the UN Charter, particularly the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity, and non-interference in the internal affairs of member states. This draft resolution is fundamentally unbalanced, seeks to engineer external regime change, and politicizes humanitarian assistance. We urge the penholder to refocus the text on facilitating inclusive, unconditioned national dialogue between all Venezuelan parties rather than deepening divisions.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution circulated by the United States. The Venezuelan people are suffering under an acute economic, political, and humanitarian crisis brought about by the illegitimate Maduro regime, and this Council must act to demand unhindered humanitarian access and peaceful, credible, free, and fair presidential elections. We stand firmly behind the democratically elected National Assembly and are ready to vote in favor of this text as drafted.

steps.summary: The United States revised the text to incorporate the fundamental humanitarian principles in OP4 and emphasize a democratic process in OP2, directly accommodating constructive proposals from European and regional partners. The delegation firmly maintained the draft's core pillars: condemning the fraudulent May 2018 elections, recognizing the National Assembly as Venezuela's sole democratically elected institution, and calling for new free, fair, and credible presidential elections. Demands from Russia and China to gut these democratic provisions and grant the illegitimate Maduro regime veto power over life-saving aid were firmly rejected.

reasons.Belgium: Belgium supports the draft resolution in line with the European Union's position, recognizing the National Assembly's democratic legitimacy, calling for free and fair presidential elections, and urging unhindered humanitarian access.
reasons.China: The draft resolution interferes in Venezuela's internal affairs, undermines its sovereignty by attempting to impose regime change and delegitimize its constitutional government, and all of China's red-line amendments were rejected by the penholder.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: While Côte d’Ivoire supports inclusive political dialogue and humanitarian assistance, it chooses to abstain in line with its non-aligned stance and A3 partners, avoiding taking sides in a polarized Council dynamic that lacks consensus.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supports a peaceful, constitutional, and democratic resolution to the crisis in Venezuela, including the entry of humanitarian aid and free and fair presidential elections, aligning with our position at the OAS and in recent Security Council deliberations.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea abstains because the draft resolution infringes upon the principles of national sovereignty and non-interference by taking sides between political institutions in Venezuela, while our key red lines regarding the recognition of the National Assembly and coordination with sovereign authorities were rejected.
reasons.France: France supports the restoration of democracy, the holding of free and fair presidential elections, and the unhindered entry of humanitarian aid into Venezuela, fully aligning with our EU partners and previous national positions.
reasons.Germany: Germany fully supports the draft resolution's call for free, fair, and credible presidential elections and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid to the Venezuelan people, in line with the position of the European Union. Germany will explain its vote after the Council has voted on the text.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia abstains because the draft resolution infringes upon principles of national sovereignty and non-interference in internal affairs by taking sides among domestic political institutions and failing to respect the need for host government consent in humanitarian delivery, with our key amendments having been rejected by the penholder.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait maintains a principled stance in favor of non-interference in internal affairs, national sovereignty, and an inclusive political dialogue between all Venezuelan parties rather than externally imposed political transitions, justifying an abstention on this text.
reasons.Peru: Peru is a leading member of the Lima Group and firmly advocates for addressing the severe humanitarian crisis in Venezuela, recognizing the democratic legitimacy of the National Assembly and calling for free, fair, and credible presidential elections. reasons.Poland: Poland aligns closely with the European Union and the United States in recognizing the democratic legitimacy of the National Assembly and calling for urgent humanitarian access and free, fair presidential elections in Venezuela.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft resolution directly targets the legitimacy of President Maduro's government, promotes unconstitutional regime change, and undermines Venezuela's sovereignty, which are explicit red lines for the Russian Federation. reasons.South Africa: South Africa votes against the draft resolution because it violates the principle of non-interference in internal affairs, undermines Venezuela's sovereignty and constitution, and seeks regime change rather than promoting genuine, inclusive national dialogue.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the US-sponsored draft resolution calling for unhindered humanitarian access and free, fair, and credible presidential elections in Venezuela, consistent with our recognition of Juan Guaidó and the National Assembly as the legitimate democratic authority.
reasons.United States of America: As the author and sponsor of the draft resolution, the United States strongly supports its adoption to address the humanitarian emergency and promote a transition to democracy through free and fair presidential elections.

before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

What we are witnessing today is not a genuine concern for the humanitarian situation in Venezuela, but another episode in the United States’ campaign of regime change. The draft resolution before us is deeply unbalanced, politically motivated, and blatantly disregards the basic norms of international law, the Charter of the United Nations, and the principle of state sovereignty. 

Under the guise of humanitarian concern, the authors of the draft seek to undermine the legitimate authorities of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, delegitimize the presidential elections of May 2018, and pave the way for foreign interference and potentially military intervention. Humanitarian assistance must never be politicized, militarized, or used as a tool to destabilize a sovereign country; it must be delivered strictly in accordance with General Assembly resolution 46/182, which explicitly requires the consent of the receiving state.

The Russian Federation advocates for a peaceful, political resolution of the situation in Venezuela through an inclusive national dialogue among Venezuelans themselves, without external ultimatums or threats. We categorically reject any attempts to impose solutions from the outside and will not allow the Security Council to be weaponized for unconstitutional regime change.
before.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States has put forward this draft resolution to address the grave humanitarian, political, and economic crisis unfolding in Venezuela. Millions of Venezuelans are suffering from severe shortages of food, medicine, and basic necessities, while millions more have been forced to flee their homeland, creating an unprecedented displacement crisis across the region.

Just days ago, the world watched in horror as the illegitimate Maduro regime used violence against peaceful, unarmed civilians and blocked trucks carrying vital food and medical supplies intended for the starving people of Venezuela. The Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of such cruelty and suffering. 

This draft resolution expresses our collective concern for the Venezuelan people, calls for unhindered humanitarian access in line with international principles, and supports a peaceful and democratic transition through free, fair, and credible presidential elections, in accordance with the Venezuelan Constitution. It affirms the role of the democratically elected National Assembly as the legitimate voice of the Venezuelan people. 

We urge all members of the Security Council to stand with the people of Venezuela and vote in favour of this resolution.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China has just voted against the draft resolution submitted by the United States. I would like to take this opportunity to explain China’s position.

China has always adhered to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations and the basic norms governing international relations. We maintain that the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of all countries must be respected, and that there must be no interference in the internal affairs of other nations. 

Venezuelan affairs must be handled and decided by the Venezuelan people themselves. China opposes external forces meddling in Venezuela’s internal affairs, and opposes any military intervention in Venezuela under any pretext. We believe that stability in Venezuela serves the fundamental interests of the Venezuelan people and is conducive to peace and stability in Latin America and the Caribbean. 

China calls on the Venezuelan Government and the opposition to seek a political solution through inclusive and peaceful dialogue within the framework of the Constitution and laws of Venezuela, so as to maintain national stability and economic and social development. The international community should provide constructive assistance to this end while strictly respecting Venezuela’s sovereignty, rather than taking actions that would escalate tensions or further complicate the situation.

With regard to the humanitarian issue, China has consistently maintained that the provision of humanitarian assistance must adhere to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, and impartiality, as well as the guiding principles set out in General Assembly resolution 46/182. Humanitarian assistance should not be politicized, nor should it be used as a pretext to serve political ends or trigger conflict. 

The draft resolution just voted upon runs counter to China’s aforementioned principled position. Therefore, China voted against it. 

China stands ready to continue to work with the international community to play a constructive role in facilitating a peaceful settlement of the Venezuelan issue.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Germany:
Mr. President,

Germany voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States, and we deeply regret that it was not adopted today.

The crisis unfolding in Venezuela is a man-made tragedy of catastrophic proportions. Millions of ordinary Venezuelans are suffering from acute shortages of food, medicine, and basic necessities, while millions more have fled their homeland, placing an enormous burden on neighboring countries across the region. 

The root cause of this humanitarian crisis is political. The presidential elections held on 20 May 2018 lacked democratic legitimacy, as they were neither free, fair, nor credible. Consequently, Germany, together with many European and international partners, has recognized the President of the democratically elected National Assembly, Juan Guaidó, as the legitimate interim President of Venezuela, tasked under the Venezuelan Constitution with organizing new, free, and transparent presidential elections. The National Assembly remains the sole democratically elected institution in the country, and the safety and constitutional prerogatives of its members must be respected.

We condemn in the strongest terms the violence and excessive use of force by security forces and armed groups against peaceful civilians. The blocking of desperately needed humanitarian aid at Venezuela’s borders is unacceptable. Humanitarian assistance must never be politicized, and it must be delivered immediately, safely, and unhindered, in strict adherence to the internationally recognized principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence.

Germany firmly believes that only a peaceful, political, and democratic solution can resolve this crisis. We reject any military options. We call for an inclusive, Venezuelan-led process that leads to credible presidential elections, in accordance with the Venezuelan Constitution. We will continue our efforts, including through the International Contact Group, to support a peaceful transition toward democracy and relief for the Venezuelan people.

Thank you.
after.Peru:
Mr. President,

Peru voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States because we believe that the Security Council cannot remain indifferent to the profound political, economic, social, and humanitarian crisis affecting Venezuela, which has generated the largest displacement crisis in the modern history of our region.

My country has welcomed more than 700,000 Venezuelans who have been forced to flee their homeland due to the severe deterioration of living conditions, the collapse of basic services, and the acute shortage of food and medicine. This is a regional crisis with direct consequences for international peace and security, and it demands an urgent, coherent, and responsible response from the international community.

We deeply regret that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this resolution, which sought to address the urgent humanitarian needs of the Venezuelan people and to support a peaceful and democratic path forward. The entry of humanitarian assistance in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence is an urgent necessity that should never be politicized or violently obstructed. The events of recent days, in which violence was used to block the delivery of vital supplies to civilians in desperate need, are unacceptable and must be condemned.

Peru reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the restoration of democracy and the constitutional order in Venezuela through a peaceful, political, and democratic process led by Venezuelans themselves, culminating in free, fair, and credible presidential elections with international observation. We recognize the legitimacy of the National Assembly as the democratically elected body representing the will of the Venezuelan people.

At the same time, we reiterate our firm conviction that this transition must be peaceful, through constitutional and political means, rejecting any course of action that involves the use of force or military intervention. 

Peru will continue to work within the Lima Group and in all multilateral forums to support the Venezuelan people and to contribute to a peaceful solution that allows Venezuela to restore its democracy, rule of law, and prosperity.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.South Africa:
Mr. President,

South Africa voted against the draft resolution contained in document S/2019/186.

South Africa remains deeply concerned by the political, economic, and humanitarian challenges facing the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela and the impact these challenges have on the Venezuelan people. However, South Africa firmly believes that any solution to the current crisis must be peaceful, Venezuelan-led, and achieved through inclusive dialogue, free from external interference, threats of force, or attempts at regime change.

South Africa voted against the draft resolution because it is unbalanced and fails to uphold the fundamental principles of the Charter of the United Nations, particularly the respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of States, as well as the principle of non-interference in matters that are essentially within the domestic jurisdiction of any State. The Security Council should not be utilized as an instrument to endorse unconstitutional changes of government or to deepen existing divisions.

Furthermore, South Africa emphasizes that humanitarian assistance must never be politicized or used as a tool for political ends. The provision of humanitarian aid must strictly adhere to the guiding principles established in General Assembly resolution 46/182, namely humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, and must be conducted in full cooperation and coordination with the legitimate authorities of the receiving State.

South Africa continues to call on all political actors in Venezuela to reject violence and commit themselves to a genuine, inclusive, and peaceful national dialogue. We encourage and support initiatives, including those by regional leaders and mechanisms such as the Montevideo Mechanism, aimed at facilitating a peaceful and negotiated political solution by the Venezuelans themselves.

I thank you, Mr. President.
